scheme_name: PMMSY: Construction of Fish Kiosks Including Kiosks of Aquarium/Ornamental Fish-Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

The scheme aims to promote sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector in India. 

One of the components of PMMSY is the construction of fish kiosks, which includes kiosks for aquarium and ornamental fish. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to enhance the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

The scheme targets a significant increase in fish production and productivity. 

The goal is to achieve an increase in fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-2025. 

This initiative also aims to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is expected to generate around 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs in the fisheries sector. 

The construction of fish kiosks is a strategic move to promote aquaculture and ornamental fish farming. 

These kiosks will serve as retail outlets for selling fresh fish and ornamental fish. 

The government aims to provide a platform for fish farmers to sell their products directly to consumers. 

This initiative is particularly beneficial for small and marginal fish farmers. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can go up to 60% of the project cost for individuals. 

For cooperative societies and groups, the assistance can be up to 80% of the project cost. 

The maximum project cost for the construction of fish kiosks is set at INR 10 lakh. 

This means that individual beneficiaries can receive financial support of up to INR 6 lakh. 

For cooperative societies, the financial support can go up to INR 8 lakh. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of Haryana. 

Applicants must be engaged in fish farming or related activities. 

There is no specific age limit mentioned for applicants. 

However, the applicant must have a valid identity proof and address proof. 

Educational qualifications are not a barrier for this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested applicants must visit the official website of the Fisheries Department of Haryana. 

They need to fill out the application form available on the website. 

The application form requires details such as name, address, and bank account information. 

Applicants must also provide details of their fish farming activities. 

Along with the application form, certain documents are required. 

These documents include a copy of the Aadhaar card, bank passbook, and proof of fish farming activity. 

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the local Fisheries Department office. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the authorities. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed to the applicant's bank account. 

The timeline for the application process can vary. 

Typically, the review process may take around 30 to 45 days. 

Disbursement of funds is expected to occur shortly after approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme in Haryana is the Fisheries Department of Haryana. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Fisheries Department can be found on the official Haryana government website. 

The PMMSY scheme also emphasizes the importance of training and capacity building. 

Beneficiaries will receive training on best practices in fish farming and kiosk management. 

This training aims to improve the skills and knowledge of fish farmers. 

The scheme also promotes the use of modern technology in fish farming. 

This includes the use of aerators and water quality management systems. 

The government aims to ensure that fish farming is environmentally sustainable. 

The construction of fish kiosks will also contribute to the local economy. 

It will provide a direct market for fish farmers to sell their products. 

This will help in reducing the dependence on middlemen. 

The initiative is expected to enhance the availability of quality fish in local markets. 

The scheme also aligns with the government's vision of "Atmanirbhar Bharat." 

It aims to make India self-reliant in fish production. 

The PMMSY scheme is part of a broader effort to boost the blue economy in India. 

The blue economy encompasses sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth. 

The government has allocated INR 20,050 crore for the PMMSY scheme over a period of five years. 

This funding will support various initiatives under the scheme, including fish kiosks. 

The scheme also aims to promote the export of fish and fish products. 

The government is targeting an increase in fish exports to INR 1 lakh crore by 2024-2025. 

The construction of fish kiosks will play a crucial role in achieving this target. 

The initiative is expected to improve the livelihoods of millions of fishers and fish farmers. 

Overall, the PMMSY scheme represents a significant investment in the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable ecosystem for fish farming in India. 

The construction of fish kiosks is a vital component of this broader initiative. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

It will empower local fish farmers and enhance their economic prospects. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to transform the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY scheme is a step towards achieving food security and nutritional needs. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of rural communities. 

The construction of fish kiosks is just one of the many initiatives under PMMSY. 

This comprehensive approach is designed to address the challenges faced by the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in rural economies across the country. 

The PMMSY scheme is a testament to the government's focus on sustainable development. 

It aims to balance economic growth with environmental conservation. 

The construction of fish kiosks is a forward-looking initiative that promises to benefit many. 

The scheme is a significant move towards enhancing fish production and productivity in India. 

It is a vital part of the government's strategy to promote aquaculture and fisheries. 

The PMMSY scheme is set to revolutionize the fisheries sector in India. 

It aims to create a robust framework for fish farming and marketing. 

The benefits of this scheme will be felt by fish farmers and consumers alike. 

The construction of fish kiosks will pave the way for a more organized fish market. 

This initiative is a crucial step towards achieving sustainable fisheries management in India.
